extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies), GHG emissions attestation providers, corporate counsel, and securities filings preparers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and disclosure standards (Regulation S-K subpart 1500 and related Form/Rule amendments) governing climate-related disclosures, GHG emissions attestation, and how those items must be presented, filed, and described in SEC filings and registration statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of GHG emissions attestation provider
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether a GHG emissions attestation provider is independent, the Commission will consider whether a relationship or the provision of a service creates a mutual or conflicting interest between the attestation provider and the registrant (or any of its affiliates), places the attestation provider in the position of attesting to such attestation provider's own work, results in the attestation provider acting as management or an employee of the registrant (or any of its affiliates), or places the attestation provider in a position of being an advocate for the registrant (or any of its affiliates); and the Commission will consider all relevant circumstances, including all financial or other relationships between the attestation provider and the registrant (or any of its affiliates), and not just those relating to reports filed with the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'affiliate' has the meaning in §210.2-01 (with 'audit' references deemed to be to attestation services). Independence evaluation covers both the period covered by the attestation report and the professional engagement period (see definition). Consider relationships and services that create conflicts, self-attestation, management roles, or advocacy; evaluate all financial and other relationships, not just SEC-report-related relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of attestation and professional engagement period
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'attestation and professional engagement period' means both: (A) the period covered by the attestation report; and (B) the period of the engagement to attest to the registrant's GHG emissions or to prepare a report filed with the Commission ('the professional engagement period'). The professional engagement period begins when the GHG attestation service provider either signs an initial engagement letter (or other agreement to attest to a registrant's GHG emissions) or begins attest procedures, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition when determining applicable conflicts, independence, timing obligations, and disclosure responsibilities that reference the engagement period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation report form and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The form and content of the attestation report must follow the requirements set forth by the attestation standard (or standards) used by the GHG emissions attestation provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the attestation report to conform with whatever attestation standard the provider is using (e.g., relevant professional/assurance standards). The rule does not prescribe a single attestation format but requires adherence to the selected attestation standard's form/content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure whether attestation provider is subject to oversight inspection programs
rubrics_metrics.description: A large accelerated filer and an accelerated filer must disclose, alongside the GHG emissions disclosure to which the attestation report relates, whether the GHG emissions attestation provider is subject to any oversight inspection program, and if so, which program (or programs), and whether the GHG emissions attestation engagement is included within the scope of authority of such oversight inspection program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request relevant information from the attestation provider as necessary to make this disclosure; include program names and whether the specific engagement falls within program scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of previous attestation provider resignations/dismissals and disagreements
rubrics_metrics.description: If any GHG emissions attestation provider that was previously engaged for the fiscal year covered by the attestation report resigned (or declined to stand for re-appointment) or was dismissed, the registrant must: (A) state whether the former provider resigned, declined to stand for re-appointment, or was dismissed and the date; and (B) state whether during the engagement there were any disagreements with the former provider on any matter of measurement or disclosure of GHG emissions or attestation scope or procedures, and if so describe each such disagreement and state whether the registrant authorized the former provider to respond fully to the successor's inquiries concerning those disagreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'disagreements' is interpreted broadly to include any difference of opinion concerning measurement or disclosure of GHG emissions or attestation scope/procedures that would have caused the former provider to reference the subject matter in its report if not resolved; it includes disagreements resolved to the former provider's satisfaction and those not resolved. Disagreements contemplated are those at the decision-making level between registrant personnel responsible for presentation and provider personnel responsible for rendering the report. An oral communication from the engagement partner or another responsible person (or designee) generally suffices as a statement of disagreement requiring disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of voluntary assurance when attestation not required
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that is not required to include a GHG emissions attestation report must disclose in the filing if the registrant's GHG emissions disclosure were subject to third-party assurance: (1) identification of the service provider of such assurance; (2) description of the assurance standard used; (3) description of the level and scope of assurance services provided; (4) brief description of the results of the assurance services; (5) whether the service provider has any material business relationships with or has provided any material professional services to the registrant; and (6) whether the service provider is subject to any oversight inspection program, and if so which program(s) and whether the assurance services over GHG emissions are included within the scope of authority of such program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these disclosure elements when voluntary third-party assurance exists even though formal attestation reporting is not required for that registrant category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location of attestation report and related disclosure in filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must include the attestation report and disclosure required by this section in the filing that contains the GHG emissions disclosure to which the report and disclosure relate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the registrant elects to incorporate by reference its GHG emissions disclosure from a Form 10-Q for the second fiscal quarter in the fiscal year immediately following the year to which the disclosure relates, or to provide the information in an amended annual report, the registrant must include an express statement in its annual report indicating its intention to incorporate by reference the attestation report from the quarterly report or to amend its annual report to provide the attestation report by the due date specified in §229.1505.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and currency for incorporation by reference of GHG emissions metrics (225-day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant is required to disclose its Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 emissions pursuant to §229.1505(a), the GHG emissions metrics disclosure that would be incorporated by reference must be as of the most recently completed fiscal year that is at least 225 days prior to the date of effectiveness of the registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing registration statements (e.g., Forms S-3, F-3), if the most recently completed fiscal year disclosure is not available within the 225-day window, incorporate by reference the prior fiscal year's GHG emissions metrics disclosure consistent with the specified timing rules. Refer to the specific Form instructions (S-3, F-3, etc.) for application details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor for forward-looking climate-related statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory safe harbors for forward-looking statements in section 27A of the Securities Act and section 21E of the Exchange Act apply as provided in this section to information provided pursuant to §§229.1502(e), 229.1502(f), 229.1502(g), and 229.1504. For purposes of this paragraph, all information required by those sections is considered a forward-looking statement for purposes of the statutory safe harbors, except for historical facts, including non-exclusive examples such as terms related to carbon offsets or RECs described pursuant to §229.1504 and statements in response to §§229.1502(e) or 229.1504 about material expenditures actually incurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat required items in the listed sections as forward-looking for safe-harbor analysis, but exclude historical-fact items (e.g., described carbon offset terms, actual expenditures incurred) from that forward-looking classification. The safe harbor also specifies certain transaction contexts (blank check companies, penny stock issuers, rollups, IPOs, certain offerings by partnerships/LLCs) where it applies as enumerated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive Data File requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the disclosure required by subpart 1500 in an Interactive Data File as required by §232.405 (Rule 405 of Regulation S-T) in accordance with the EDGAR Filer Manual (see §232.301).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and submit the climate-related disclosure in the required interactive data format (EDGAR XML/inline XBRL or other formats as specified) consistent with the EDGAR Filer Manual and Rule 405 specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of limited assurance attestation reports under Rule 436(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding provisions about consents required in special cases, the following shall not be considered part of the registration statement prepared or certified by a person within the meaning of sections 7 and 11 of the Act: (1) A report by an attestation provider covering Scope 1, Scope 2, and/or Scope 3 GHG emissions at a limited assurance level; and (2) Any description of assurance regarding a registrant's GHG emissions disclosure provided in accordance with §229.1506(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited assurance attestation reports and certain assurance descriptions are treated as not part of the registration statement for the purposes of determining who prepared or certified the registration statement under sections 7 and 11; this affects consent/ liability considerations in registration contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-specific captioning and cross-referencing requirements for climate-related disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms and registration statements (e.g., Form S-1 Part I Item 11(o); Form S-11 Item 9; Form 10 Item 3.A; Form 20-F Item 3.E; Form 10-Q Item 1B; Form 10-K Item 6; and corresponding instructions for S-3, S-4, F-3, F-4) must provide the information required by subpart 1500 in a part of the filing that is separately captioned as 'Climate-Related Disclosure.' A registrant may include responsive disclosure in other parts of the filing (e.g., Risk Factors, Business, MD&A), but should consider whether cross-referencing those disclosures in the separately captioned section would enhance presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When completing Forms and registration statements, include a separately captioned 'Climate-Related Disclosure' section or clearly cross-reference climate-related disclosures located elsewhere in the filing to improve investor presentation and compliance with the Form instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 20-F exhibit letter re GHG emissions attestation report
rubrics_metrics.description: Letter re GHG emissions attestation report: A letter, where applicable, from the GHG emissions attestation provider that acknowledges awareness of the use in a registration statement of a GHG emissions attestation report that pursuant to Rule 436(i)(1) is not considered a part of a registration statement prepared or certified by a person within the meaning of sections 7 and 11 of the Securities Act. Such letter may be filed with the Form 20-F if the Form 20-F is incorporated by reference into a Securities Act registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider filing an acknowledgment letter from the attestation provider with Form 20-F where the Form 20-F will be incorporated by reference into a Securities Act registration statement, to document the provider's awareness of Rule 436(i)(1) treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction regarding limited assurance and Form 20-F exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction 1 to Item 1506: A registrant that obtains assurance from an attestation provider at the limited assurance level should refer to §229.601(b)(27) and paragraph 18 of Form 20-F's Instructions as to Exhibits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the referenced Form 20-F exhibit instructions and §229.601(b)(27) when limited assurance is obtained to ensure correct exhibit treatment and cross-references in filings.
